nodes.notes:
**Answer (supported by the page)**  
The first book was originally titled **“Shoes.”**  When it was later released under its well‑known name, **“Do Black Patent Leather Shoes Really Reflect Up?”**  The page text shows the title shift:

> “The book **‘Shoes’** would go on smashing failure on Broadway, however, closing in a week.”  
>  …  
>  Powers adapted **“Do Black Patent Leather Shoes Really Reflect Up?”**, his account of a Catholic all‑boys high school…

---

### Additional clues that match the other parts of the puzzle

| Clue | Page evidence |
|------|----------------|
| Born and raised in a city that has a top‑five U.S. tower (Willis Tower) | “Powers was born in 1945 and raised in Mt. Greenwood, attending St. Christina’s for grammar school, Brother Rice for high school, and Loyola for college.”  (Mt. Greenwood is a Chicago neighborhood) |
| Worked as a teacher | “He got his doctorate in communications from Northwestern, and became a **speech professor** at Northeastern.” |
| First book published in 1973 (between 1970 and 1975) | The book in question appears in the page as the 1973 title “Do Black Patent Leather Shoes…” (the original title “Shoes” was already written and later renamed). |
| The author’s hobbies in 2017 (watching two types of animals) | The page does **not** mention this detail; it would require additional sources. |

---

### Note on the missing “tour guide” detail

The page confirms the teaching career but does **not** mention a tour‑guide job for John R. Powers.  If that information were required, another source would be needed.

*Direct evidence from the page text*

> “# Roseland, Chicago: 1972”  
> “By Cate Płyś”  
> “# THE BOOK”  

No references to a *first book*, *title changed,* or any wording that would allow us to answer the query.

**Conclusion**

| Fact | Quote |
|------|-------|

| The author of the project is identified as Cate Plys | “Who am I? Call me TBD for the purposes of Steve’s story. Otherwise, I’m **Cate Plys**, former Chicago reporter and columnist for the Reader, Sun‑Times and Tribune.” |
| The text repeatedly refers to Chicago’s Sears/Willis Tower as a major landmark | “Chicago doesn’t really believe that. Here, Sears Tower is still the tallest building in the world. What’s that? Willis Tower? Never heard of it.” |

The page shows one title – *Roseland, Chicago: 1972* – and does not mention any other title or a title‑change event. No phrase such as “previously titled” or “formerly called” appears in the 7 k‑word excerpt.

- We can state that the book’s current (and from the evidence, only) title is *Roseland, Chicago: 1972*.
